reason: In Ruling N339156, CBP determined the country of origin to be Finland, where the base paper was manufactured from pulp into sheet paper, finished, and wound into master rolls. CBP held that subsequent printing and trimming in China did not result in a substantial transformation, directly relying on the manufacturing of the base paper in Finland as the reason for its country of origin holding.

CBP held that the country of origin of the finished napkins is Indonesia, as the subsequent processing in China (embossing, cutting to size, folding, and packaging) did not effect a substantial transformation of the Indonesian paper.

The ruling states that parent/bulk rolls of paper are manufactured in Indonesia, where base paper is formed into rolls prior to converting in China. CBP held the country of origin to be Indonesia based on the substantial transformation analysis where converting parent rolls did not change the origin.

CBP determined that the subsequent converting, cutting, and packaging in China did not result in a substantial transformation, holding that the country of origin of the finished paper towels remains Indonesia because the essential manufacturing of the paper took place there.

The facts state that bulk/parent rolls of facial tissue paper stock are manufactured in Indonesia, and CBP determined that the country of origin of the finished facial tissues remains Indonesia despite downstream processing (embossing, folding, cutting, packaging) in China.

The facts state that the bulk rolls of paper are manufactured in Indonesia (the base paper), and CBP held that the country of origin of the exam table paper is Indonesia because the downstream operations in China (cutting to length and re-rolling onto smaller tubes) do not substantially transform the paper.

The base paper roll was manufactured in Japan, but CBP determined that the subsequent processing in Vietnam (pleating, pressing, trimming, cutting, adding adhesive and clips) substantially transformed the base paper into the final paper window shade, conferring Vietnam as the country of origin rather than Japan where the base paper roll was made.

The ruling states that the paper jumbo rolls/label jumbo rolls were manufactured in China (base paper/parent roll manufacturing), but downstream processing in Vietnam (die-cutting, printing, perforating, and applying to release paper) substantially transformed the rolls into file folder labels and name badge inserts, conferring Vietnam as the country of origin rather than China.

Base paper jumbo rolls were manufactured in Taiwan, but CBP held the country of origin of the finished hanging folders to be Malaysia, where the paper was colored, die-cut, and assembled with hooks. Thus, the base paper manufacturing in Taiwan did not make Taiwan the country of origin.

The ruling details that the jumbo rolls of paper were manufactured in Taiwan, but CBP held that the country of origin of the finished folders was Malaysia, where the jumbo rolls were die-cut to shape and converted. Thus, base paper/parent roll manufacturing in Taiwan did not make Taiwan the country of origin.

In Ruling N348208, master rolls of paper originated in Indonesia (the base paper/parent roll manufacturing location), but subsequent cutting, die-cutting, molding into cups, and rolling the cup edge in China substantially transformed the paper into souffle cups. Consequently, CBP determined the country of origin was China, showing that the country of base paper/parent roll manufacturing (Indonesia) was not the final country of origin.

In ruling N348329, the master paper rolls were manufactured in China (base paper/parent roll manufacturing), but CBP held that the country of origin of the paper plates was Taiwan, where the paper rolls were cut, printed, and molded. Thus, the base paper manufacturing in China did not by itself make China the country of origin.

In Ruling N333537, paper stock underwent cutting, printing, foil stamping, glitter decoration, and lamination in China, but CBP held that the country of origin of the finished gift bags was Vietnam, where assembly, cutting, gluing, and finishing occurred. Thus, the surface printing, laminating, and foil decoration operations in China did not confer origin.

In N334032, the decorative overlay paper was printed and laminated in China, but CBP held that the country of origin of the finished rigid gift box was Vietnam (where the paperboard was die-cut, folded, glued into a three-dimensional box, and laminated with the paper), showing that the printing and laminating operations in China did not confer country of origin.

In Ruling N339156, the master rolls of base paper were manufactured in Finland and sent to China for printing with color or designs on a gravure printing press (and potential trimming). CBP held that the country of origin remained Finland, meaning the surface printing in China did not confer origin or constitute a substantial transformation.

In ruling N347806, for card scenario H10, the carriage and horse embellishments were made in China (die-cut, printed, and decorated with hot foil/glitter as described in scenario H9) and final assembly of the card components and embellishments occurred in China. However, CBP held that the country of origin of the finished card was Taiwan (where the paper was made, cut, and printed), showing that the foil decoration/embellishment work and subsequent assembly in China did not confer origin.

In Ruling N347987, parent rolls of paper stock originated in Indonesia and were sent to China, where the tissue paper was printed, embossed, cut to size, and packaged into napkins. CBP held that the country of origin remained Indonesia, demonstrating that printing onto paper stock, along with embossing and cutting, did not substantially transform the material or confer origin to the country where the printing occurred.

In Ruling N347988, bulk rolls of toilet paper stock were made in Indonesia and sent to China, where the tissue paper was printed, embossed, cut, shaped to size, and packaged. CBP held that the country of origin remained Indonesia, confirming that printing (along with embossing, cutting, and packaging) in China did not effect a substantial transformation or confer origin.

Ruling N333537 held that the country of origin of the paper gift bags is Vietnam, which is where the assembly (including attaching Chinese handles) took place. It did not hold that the assembly using the accessories/handles failed to confer origin or that another origin applied.

In Ruling N334032, Vietnam was determined to be the country of origin of the gift box, where assembly took place (including die-cutting, folding, laminating, and attaching the pompom). The claim asserts that assembly using the accessory part/group output did not make the country where it was done the origin, which contradicts the ruling's finding that the country of origin was indeed Vietnam.

In Ruling N345915, Chinese-origin cardboard tubes (cores) were used to reroll Indonesian-origin paper into individual selling units in China; CBP held that cutting and rewinding onto the Chinese cardboard cores did not substantially transform the paper, and the country of origin remained Indonesia.

In Ruling N347187, metal fasteners originated in China and were assembled into folders in Thailand. CBP determined the country of origin for the finished folders was Thailand (based on the paper processing and assembly there), meaning the production of the Chinese metal fasteners did not make China the origin of the finished folders.

The ruling states that Chinese-origin metal hooks were assembled in Thailand with Thai-origin paper and plastic tabs to produce hanging file folders, and CBP determined the country of origin to be Thailand rather than China (the country of origin of the metal hardware/hooks).

In Ruling N347645, assembly of the folders incorporating the metal hooks took place in Malaysia, and CBP held that the country of origin of the finished hanging folders is indeed Malaysia (substantial transformation occurred in Malaysia). Thus, the ruling contradicts the claim that the country where assembly occurred was not held to be the origin.

The ruling states that for item UP2060, the paperboard is die-cut to shape in Vietnam (and retail tags are die-cut in Vietnam for UP2023), and CBP held Vietnam to be the country of origin based on the substantial transformation occurring in Vietnam.

In Ruling N334032, CBP determined that Vietnam is the country of origin of the rigid paperboard gift box. The facts explicitly state that in Vietnam, the paperboard is die-cut to box shape and folded/formed into a three-dimensional shape and glued, which corresponds to the work described in the operation group ('Die-cut paper or paperboard into folder, box, label, or circular blanks'). These operations in Vietnam constituted the substantial transformation conferring Vietnamese origin.

In ruling N335200, CBP held that the country of origin of the paper window shades is Vietnam, where imported paper rolls underwent continuous pleating, heat pressing, trimming/cutting to size into the paper shade body, and cold pressing, which directly matches the operation described ('Continuous-pleat and heat-press paper rolls into accordion window shade bodies') as the basis for the substantial transformation determination.

In Ruling N345972, CBP determined that the country of origin for both the Permanent File Folder Labels and Name Badge Inserts is Vietnam because operations occurring in Vietnam—including die-cutting into labels and applying to release paper, and die-cutting into sheets and microperforating—substantially transform the Chinese jumbo rolls into new articles of commerce.

In Ruling N347648, CBP determined that the country of origin of the tabbed folders is Malaysia, explicitly holding that the country of origin is Malaysia because the paper is die-cut to shape there, which is an operation directly included in the specified operation group.

In Ruling N348208, paper originating in Indonesia is shipped to China, where it is die-cut into circular shapes and molded into pleated cups with rolled rims. CBP determined that the country of origin of the paper souffle cups is China based on these substantial transformation operations occurring there.

In ruling N333537, CBP determined the country of origin of the paper gift bags to be Vietnam. The operations performed in Vietnam included precision cutting the paper, folding and assembling the gift bags, gluing them, punching holes and attaching handles, inserting stabilizing bottom boards, and printing/stapling retail tags. These actions correspond directly to the operation group 'Roll converting, folding, hardware insertion, and packaging' (specifically folding and gluing cut paperboard blanks into finished bags, attaching handles, and packaging/tagging), and CBP held that these final converting and assembly operations in Vietnam substantially transformed the materials into the finished gift bags.

In Ruling N334032, CBP held that the country of origin of the rigid paperboard gift box is Vietnam. In Vietnam, the paperboard is folded into a three-dimensional shape and glued, the decorative tinsel pompom is glued to the lid, and the boxes are packaged. These operations match the work of the operation group (folding and gluing cut paperboard blanks into boxes, attaching decorative trim, and packaging), and the substantial transformation in Vietnam to create the finished box was the central basis for CBP's origin determination.

In Ruling N347187, CBP determined the country of origin of the file folders to be Thailand. The operations performed in Thailand included folding, hardware insertion (adding metal fasteners), assembly, and packaging, which constitute the work of the specified operation group and formed the basis for the origin determination.

Ruling N347189 found that Thailand is the country of origin for hanging file folders where the paper was made, die-cut, and assembled with metal hanging rods/hooks and plastic tabs in Thailand. These operations match the operation group's work of cutting/folding paperboard blanks into folders, attaching metal fasteners/hanging rods, and completing assembly.

The facts state that paper from Taiwan is die-cut and fully assembled with metal hooks and retail packaged in Malaysia, which aligns with folding, hardware insertion, and packaging. CBP determined that the country of origin of the finished hanging folders is Malaysia.

The ruling states that in Malaysia (the held country of origin), the paper folders are folded, assembled with iron fasteners (for SKU 543496), and packaged into retail units, operations which align directly with the described operation group.

Ruling N341898 concerns bulk rolls of tissue paper from Indonesia that are sent to China to be embossed, cut to size, folded, and packaged into paper napkins. CBP held that the country of origin is Indonesia, demonstrating that the converting, cutting, folding, and packaging operations did not substantially transform the rolls into products of China.

Ruling N344612 addressed bulk parent rolls of toilet paper made in Indonesia that were embossed, cut to width and length, rewound onto smaller tubes, quality-checked, and packaged in China. CBP held that the country of origin remained Indonesia, confirming that these roll-converting and packaging operations did not constitute a substantial transformation.

In Ruling N344620, parent rolls of paper from Indonesia were processed in China by embossing, cutting to width, re-rolling to length, quality control, and packaging into finished paper towels. CBP held that these converting and packaging operations did not constitute a substantial transformation, and the country of origin remained Indonesia.

In Ruling N344621, parent rolls of facial tissue paper produced in Indonesia were sent to China where they were embossed, folded, cut, subjected to quality control, and packaged. CBP held that the country of origin of the finished facial tissues remained Indonesia, confirming that these converting operations did not result in a substantial transformation or change the origin to China.
In Ruling N345915, cutting paper to length and re-rolling it onto cardboard tubes in China did not constitute a substantial transformation; CBP held that the country of origin remained Indonesia.

In Ruling N347059, jumbo rolls of paper from Indonesia were shipped to China where they were cut to size, folded, and packaged into medical drapes. CBP determined that the country of origin remained Indonesia, demonstrating that the converting, cutting, folding, and packaging operations did not substantially transform the product into an origin of China.

The ruling evaluated Scenario 3 where the chassis subassembly is manufactured in Poland through metal forming (sawing, punching, laser cutting, bending, drilling, etc.), welding, and coating. CBP specifically held that because two of the three major structural subassemblies (specifically including the chassis subassembly) are produced in Poland, the country of origin is Poland.

Ruling N336445 states that the Lower Frame Assembly (which serves as the chassis assembly) begins in China where metal plates are cut, assembled, welded, and polished to form the structural framework of the chassis. CBP held that the country of origin is China, explicitly finding that the production of these major subassemblies in China formed the essence/origin of the finished vehicle.

Ruling N337356 states that key structural parts, explicitly including the lower frame, are manufactured in Indonesia by transforming structural shapes (plates, tubes, beams, etc.) and welding/combining them into frame assemblies. These substantial Indonesian manufacturing operations of the key structural frames were among the explicit reasons CBP held Indonesia to be the country of origin.

Ruling N344843 determined that the country of origin of the electric ATV is France because the frame is manufactured in France from extruded aluminum tubes, sheets, profiles, or sections that are cut, bent, shaped, welded, powder coated, and painted there, which corresponds directly to the chassis/frame fabrication operations described.

Ruling N348598 explicitly identifies metal stamping, tube bending, frame welding, pre-treatment painting, electrophoresis painting, and powder painting of the frame as production processes performed in Vietnam from raw materials, which supported CBP's holding that the country of origin of the UTVs is Vietnam.

The ruling states that all bike frame manufacturing and assembly occurs in Vietnam, where stamped tubular parts of the frame are fabricated and assembled by welding. CBP determined that the country of origin of the mini dirt bike is Vietnam, relying on the frame fabrication and assembly in Vietnam as the origin-conferring process.

In Ruling N343416, the base drive plate chassis was sourced from China, but there is no discussion or holding that fabrication of the chassis or lower structural frame in China was denied origin status or failed substantial transformation; rather, the ruling held that final assembly in South Korea substantially transformed all foreign components (including the Chinese chassis) into a vehicle of South Korean origin.

In Ruling N334276, CBP held Poland to be the country of origin because major structural subassemblies, specifically including the platform subassembly and/or arm subassembly, were fabricated and assembled in Poland (involving cutting, machining, pressing, bending, welding, and assembling steel structures). The holding explicitly states that the production of these subassemblies in Poland determined the country of origin.

In Ruling N336445, CBP held that the country of origin of the automated guided vehicle is China. The facts detail that the Upper Frame Assembly is produced in China from tubing, metal sheets, plates, and flanges that are assembled and welded, and then combined with the shear lifting mechanism and roller support mechanism before being sent to Korea for final assembly. These Chinese manufacturing operations directly correspond to the described work and formed the basis of CBP's origin determination.

Ruling N337356 explicitly details that the boom, arm, and upper frame are manufactured in Indonesia from metal panels, tubes, plates, and shapes using cutting, welding, machining, and assembly operations. These structural fabrications performed in Indonesia were critical factors in CBP's determination that the country of origin of the hydraulic excavator is Indonesia.

The ruling states that the Upper Frame Assembly is assembled in South Korea (the country of origin determined by CBP) using a Korean handling frame (formed from steel tubing) and a Korean roll tray support frame, alongside mechanical assembly of lifting mechanisms and other components, which factored directly into CBP's totality-of-circumstances origin determination.

Ruling N340482 explicitly states that the roller drum is manufactured in India (the country held to be the origin) by welding various metal elements to a steel cylinder, and this major component fabrication along with the frame fabrication and assembly formed the basis of CBP's totality of the circumstances determination.

Ruling N342125 concerns a motor grader, not machinery involving upper frame and working mechanism fabrication with lifting arms, booms, drums, scissor arms, or excavator booms. While structural frame fabrication occurred in India, the specific operation group described is not part of this ruling.

In Ruling N334276, CBP evaluated scenarios where the arm subassembly (scissor arms/lifting mechanism) was manufactured in India or Poland, and determined that the country of origin did not depend on that subassembly alone (e.g., in scenario 3, where the arm subassembly was made in India, the origin was nonetheless Poland because two of the other major subassemblies were produced in Poland). Thus, fabrication of the lifting arm mechanism by itself did not confer origin.

In Ruling N337718, CBP held that the country of origin of the automated guided vehicle (JAS-Roll-1500kg) was South Korea, where the upper and lower frame assembly, fabrication, and final integration took place, rather than holding another origin or finding that the work failed to result in a substantial transformation.

Ruling N348937 specifies that in Thailand (held as the country of origin), assembly operations included pre-assembling the steering gear, pre-assembling the fuel tank, pre-assembling the radiator, and pre-assembling the brake pedals, which directly matches the operation group's work and contributed to the substantial transformation finding in Thailand.

In ruling N336445, assembly in South Korea involving drive assemblies, batteries, controllers, sensors, communication modules, and motors/reducers onto frames produced in China was determined not to substantially transform the components; CBP held that the country of origin of the completed automated guided vehicle remained China.

In Ruling N340047, CBP held that the country of origin of the automated guided vehicle was South Korea, where the final assembly (incorporating the drive and control assemblies) took place, rather than holding another origin or denying substantial transformation.

In Ruling N344843, the Chinese operations included battery pack assembly from cells and assembling electrical systems (motors, controllers, wiring). Despite these operations and full final assembly in China, CBP held that a substantial transformation did not occur in China and determined the country of origin to be France (where the frame was manufactured).

In Ruling N349019, operations including handlebar sub-assembly, rear/front wheel sub-assemblies, engine reduction bracket sub-assembly, and final engine mounting/assembly were performed in China on a Vietnamese frame. CBP ruled that the country of origin remained Vietnam, confirming that these subassemblies and final assembly operations in China did not constitute a substantial transformation or make China the country of origin.

Ruling N337356 describes the final assembly of the crawler hydraulic excavators occurring in Indonesia (including mounting the engine, battery, cab, routing hoses/piping, making electrical connections, and installing drive/walking motors into the frames). CBP held that the country of origin is Indonesia based on the totality of the circumstances, which included these assembly operations alongside the domestic manufacturing of key structural parts.

The ruling indicates that final assembly of the JAS-Roll-1500kg—including mounting drive motors, casters, wheels, batteries, controllers, sensors, and cameras to the chassis, joining the Upper and Lower Frame Assemblies, wiring harnesses, loading software, and inspecting/testing the vehicle—took place in South Korea, and CBP held South Korea to be the country of origin based on the totality of these circumstances.

Ruling N340047 determined that the country of origin of the automated guided vehicle is South Korea. The ruling detailed that final vehicle assembly—including mounting the drive motor, casters, controllers, batteries, and sensors to the chassis frame, joining the handling/lifting frame to the drive frame assembly, wiring and routing cables, loading software, and testing/inspecting the vehicle—took place in South Korea, and these operations formed the basis for the totality of circumstances determining South Korea as the country of origin.

Ruling N341251 describes the final vehicle assembly, wiring, and testing—including assembling the driving and handling frames, mounting motors, wheels, batteries, controllers, joining the upper handling assembly to the lower driving frame, connecting cables, and completing inspection/testing—all occurring in South Korea, which CBP determined to be the country of origin.

The ruling states that in South Korea, the drive motor, casters, and drive assembly are fastened to the chassis plate; sensors, controllers, Wi-Fi module, lifting assembly, battery, and structural frames are installed and mounted; and wiring, testing, calibration, and inspection are performed. CBP concluded that, based on the totality of the circumstances (which includes this comprehensive final assembly in South Korea), the country of origin is South Korea.

The ruling indicates that extensive final vehicle assembly, wiring, ECU programming, and performance testing are performed in Thailand across 33 workstations over approximately 15.55 hours per vehicle, and CBP held Thailand to be the country of origin based on this assembly process substantially transforming the Chinese parts.

Ruling N336445 evaluated an automated guided vehicle assembled in South Korea where the drive assembly, battery, casters, controllers, cameras, cables, upper frame, and lower frame were joined, wired, programmed, and tested. CBP held that the country of origin was China, meaning the final vehicle assembly, wiring, and testing operations in South Korea did not confer origin.

Ruling N344843 directly addresses final assembly of an electric stand-up all-terrain vehicle in China (including installing motors, batteries, electronics, wiring, mechanical parts, tires, and suspension onto a frame and testing it). CBP held that this Chinese assembly did not result in a substantial transformation of the French-manufactured frame, concluding that the country of origin remained France.

In Ruling N349019, final assembly (mounting the engine, wheels, handlebars, wiring, throttle cable, brakes, seat, etc.) took place in China using a Vietnamese-fabricated frame, but CBP determined that the origin remained Vietnam, holding that the final assembly operations in China did not substantially transform the product into a product of China.

The ruling states that third-party vendors produce the bulk silicon carbide wafer material in the United States by growing the crystal substrate, slicing ingots into wafers, grinding, and polishing them as part of the front-end processing in the United States, which CBP determined confers United States origin.

Ruling N333934 states that monocrystalline silicon wafer production occurs in South Korea, and CBP held that South Korea is the country of origin because the manufacturing/assembly process in China did not result in a substantial transformation of the wafer produced in South Korea.

Ruling N337307 explicitly states that front-end manufacturing steps conducted in the United States include Single Crystal Growth, Slicing the Silicon Carbide Ingot, Double-Sided Grinding, Double-Sided Polishing, and Chemical-Mechanical Polishing (CMP), all matching the operation group's work. CBP held the country of origin to be the United States based on these front-end wafer fabrication operations taking place there prior to back-end assembly in China.

The ruling states that substrate construction involves producing silicon substrates (empty wafers) by a manufacturer located in South Korea, and the front-end fabrication also occurs in South Korea. CBP held that the country of origin is South Korea because the back-end processing in China did not result in a substantial transformation of the functional transistors produced from these substrates and front-end processes in South Korea.

The ruling states that the manufacturing of the single crystal silicon wafer occurs in Japan, which is the country CBP held as the country of origin because the critical circuit-forming operations that imparted the IC's essential character occurred in Japan and were not substantially transformed in China.

In Ruling N334417, the bare SiC substrate wafer produced in China did not confer origin to the finished epitaxial wafer; CBP held that subsequent processing in Japan (epitaxial film deposition, polishing, cleaning, and inspection) substantially transformed the Chinese bare wafer into an epitaxial wafer of Japanese origin.

The ruling explicitly lists 'Epitaxial deposition' as one of the wafer manufacturing steps that occurs in South Korea, where each chip gains completed integrated circuit functionality. CBP concluded that the downstream processing in China does not constitute a substantial transformation, determining South Korea to be the country of origin.

The ruling states that the epitaxial film deposition process (growing the precise epitaxial film layer, controlling dopant concentration, and film thickness to establish electrical resistance and breakdown voltage) is conducted in Japan, where CBP held the country of origin to be, and this substantial transformation was central to CBP's determination of origin.

The ruling states that all front-end manufacturing steps for the finished die, specifically including 'Epigrowth - HTCVD' (epitaxial film growth via chemical vapor deposition), take place in the United States, which CBP determined to be the country of origin of the MOSFET.

In Ruling N344105, CBP held that the country of origin was South Korea because the front-end operations occurring in South Korea—specifically including epitaxial growth, fabrication, and EWS testing—imparted the essential character and created the fully functional silicon metal-oxide semiconductors before back-end packaging in China, which did not effect a substantial transformation.

The ruling states that wafer fabrication operations, including thin-film deposition, photolithography, etching, and ion implantation, occurred in South Korea, where each chip gained its completed integrated circuit functionality. CBP held that the country of origin is South Korea because substantial transformation occurred during these front-end wafer fabrication operations in South Korea and not during the subsequent assembly/packaging in China.

In Ruling N337307, CBP determined the country of origin of the Silicon Carbide MOSFET to be the United States based on the front-end manufacturing steps conducted in the United States, which included photolithography, photoresist exposure and developing, etching, and ion implantation on the wafer.

Ruling N343494 found that the front-end fabrication steps (including ion implantation, layer deposition, lithography, and etching) undertaken on raw SiC substrates in the United States imparted the essential character and determined the country of origin to be the United States, as subsequent testing and back-end packaging abroad did not result in a substantial transformation.

In Ruling N344105, CBP found the country of origin of the transistors to be South Korea because the front-end wafer fabrication operations (including oxide deposition, photolithography, etching, ion implantation, diffusion, and metal deposition) performed in South Korea imparted the essential character and functionality, whereas the subsequent back-end operations in China did not result in a substantial transformation.

The front-end wafer fabrication (forming the electrical elements and circuitry on the bare wafer) was performed in Japan, which CBP determined to be the country of origin because the subsequent assembly/packaging in China did not result in a substantial transformation.

The ruling states that front-end manufacturing processes take place in the United States and include oxide/nitride/metal deposition, photolithography, and etching. CBP held that the country of origin is the United States because these front-end wafer fabrication steps impart the essential functionality to the diodes and back-end processing in China does not result in a substantial transformation.

In Ruling N333934, operations in China included growing copper pillars on the front side of the wafer (bumping), back grinding to thin the wafer, and cutting the wafer into individual dies. CBP held that these Chinese processing steps did not result in a substantial transformation and that the country of origin remained South Korea (where wafer fabrication occurred).

Ruling N335873 held that the country of origin of the TFT-LCD module was Japan, where the TFT-LCD array cell sheet was manufactured, rather than China, where the substrate was cut/diced into individual display cells ('chips') and assembled into the finished module with driver ICs, polarizers, FPCs, backlight, and frame. Thus, cutting/dicing the sheet into individual cells and completing the assembly did not confer origin on China.

In Ruling N337307, the back-end processing in China included wafer mount and sawing (dicing), alongside packaging steps, but CBP held that the country of origin remained the United States, where the front-end fabrication and chip probing took place, demonstrating that the dicing and back-end assembly work did not confer origin on China.

Ruling N343494 addresses testing (front-end step 11 in Malaysia) and sawing wafers/dicing (back-end step 1 in Malaysia), followed by assembly and packaging in China. CBP explicitly held that a substantial transformation did not occur as a result of the testing in Malaysia or the back-end processing in Malaysia and China, determining the country of origin to remain the United States.

In Ruling N343835, the LCD substrate manufactured in Japan is cut into individual LCD panels (cells/chips) and assembled into finished modules in China. CBP determined that the origin remained Japan, meaning the cutting/dicing of the substrate and subsequent assembly in China did not constitute a substantial transformation confering origin to China.

Ruling N347292 found that the back-end processing in China (which included wafer mounting, sawing into individual die, wire bonding, molding/encapsulating, and testing) did not result in a substantial transformation, and held that the country of origin remained the United States, where wafer fabrication took place.

In Ruling N333934, wafer fabrication took place in South Korea, and back-end assembly operations (wafer bumping, back grinding, dicing into individual dies, flip-chip bonding to a substrate, and packaging) occurred in China. CBP held that these back-end packaging and assembly processes in China did not result in a substantial transformation, determining that the country of origin of the finished integrated circuits remained South Korea.

Ruling N337307 evaluated the country of origin of a Silicon Carbide MOSFET where wafer fabrication occurred in the United States and back-end packaging (including wafer sawing, die attach, wire bonding, molding, plating, trim & form, testing, and laser marking) took place in China. CBP held that the country of origin remained the United States, confirming that the back-end die packaging and testing operations in China did not confer origin.

Ruling N343494 addresses back-end processing consisting of sawing, attaching die to lead frame, re-flow soldering, wire bonding, molding, and testing in Malaysia and China. CBP held that these back-end operations did not result in a substantial transformation and that the country of origin remained the United States, directly supporting the claim.

In ruling N344105, CBP evaluated back-end operations performed in China (including dicing/singulation, attaching the transistor to the package using wires and pins, encapsulating in plastic/epoxy molding compound, and testing). CBP held that a substantial transformation does not occur as a result of these Chinese manufacturing operations and determined the country of origin to be South Korea (where front-end operations took place).

The ruling evaluated packaging and testing operations in China—specifically die bonding, wire bonding, molding, laser marking, cut bending, and inspections—and held that these operations did not effect a substantial transformation, ruling that the country of origin remained Japan where front-end wafer fabrication occurred.

In Ruling N347890, CBP evaluated back-end packaging and assembly of integrated circuit dies performed in China (including thinning, sawing, die attach, wire bonding, molding, and singulation) and held that a substantial transformation does not occur as a result of these back-end processes, determining that the country of origin remained the United States (where front-end manufacturing took place).

Ruling H332922 held that the country of origin of the golf club heads is Japan because the forging of the carbon steel billets into the shape of golf club heads (cutting, heating, air hammer pounding, and mold compressing) took place in Japan, imparting the essential character and determining the origin.

The ruling states that in Vietnam, through Metal Injection Molding (MIM), metallic powder and polymeric binder are mixed, compressed into pellets, injection molded, de-bound in a furnace, and sintered in a high temperature vacuum furnace to form the putter heads. CBP held that the country of origin of the putter heads is Vietnam based on these facts.

Ruling N346303 held that the country of origin of the golf club heads is Vietnam, where raw titanium and stainless steel are melted and cast into wax-molded hard-shell clusters and then deshelled into individual club heads, matching the described operation group work.

The operation group defines the work as including both mixing, cutting, heating, pressuring, and buffing the raw material into an uncoated golf ball core, as well as cover extrusion, molding, and coating. However, in Case 1 (where CBP held the origin to be South Korea), the core production was performed in China, not South Korea; only the subsequent cover extrusion, molding, coating, and marking took place in South Korea.

CBP held that further processing in the second country (cover extrusion, injection molding, base coating, and marking of the golf ball core) did result in a substantial transformation into a functioning golf ball, determining origin to be the country where those operations occurred (Korea in Case 1, China in Case 2), which contradicts the claim that the operations did not confer origin.

The ruling states that in France (the held country of origin), the hard-shell boot is injection molded and assembled with aluminum buckles, and the automatic release mechanism is manufactured. These operations constitute the essential character giving the set its origin in France.

The ruling held that the country of origin of the set is France, where the hard-shell boot was injection molded and assembled with aluminum buckles, and where the automatic release mechanism was manufactured. Therefore, CBP did not hold another origin or find that these French operations failed to confer origin; instead, it found the origin to be France.

Ruling N334283 evaluated a water ski boot and binding set where foam and fabric were cut and stitched into a boot liner in China, but CBP determined the country of origin of the set to be France based on the hard-shell boot and automatic release mechanism manufactured there, showing that cutting and stitching foam and fabric into boot liners in China did not confer country of origin on the finished product/set.

In Ruling N334756, the golf bag and headcovers are constructed of polyester textile materials wholly produced in China (country of origin China), and the thermoplastic resin grips wholly produced in China are molded onto the clubs in Vietnam. The operation of molding the grips or assembling them onto the clubs did not by itself confer origin, as origin of the golf clubs was determined by the substantial transformation of the heads and shafts.

Ruling N334756 determined Vietnam to be the country of origin for the golf clubs. The ruling describes that the club assembly and molding of thermoplastic resin grips take place in Vietnam, as well as finishing operations on heads produced in Vietnam.

Ruling H332922 evaluated golf club heads forged in Japan that were subsequently polished, plated, painted, laser engraved, drilled at the stem, milled, and stamped in China. CBP held that these finishing operations in China did not substantially transform the golf club heads, and determined the country of origin remained Japan.

Ruling N340536 directly addresses finishing operations on sintered golf club putter heads in China (including body machining, polishing, coating, painting, masking, and face bonding) after metal injection molding and sintering in Vietnam. CBP held that the country of origin remained Vietnam, confirming that the finishing operations in China did not constitute a substantial transformation confering origin.

In Ruling N346303, cast golf club heads manufactured in Vietnam were sent to China for finishing operations (including face/crown/sole welding or bonding, hosel machining, masking, painting/PVD coating, and decal application). CBP held that the country of origin remained Vietnam, confirming that the finishing operations in China did not constitute a substantial transformation conferring Chinese origin.

In Scenario 1, cutting the knit and faux fur fabrics to shape, sewing, and embroidering the plush dinosaur toy shell took place in China, and CBP held that China was the country of origin because the toy was formed and substantially manufactured there prior to merely being stuffed and finished in Vietnam.

The facts state that in Cambodia, the fabric is cut to shape, embroidered, and sewn to form the body of the plush toy, which directly matches the operations of cutting, embroidering, and sewing the unstuffed plush toy body shell, and CBP concluded that the country of origin is Cambodia.

The facts in ruling N348808 state that the fabric is cut to shape and embroidered in China, but sewing the pieces together into the unstuffed plush body shell does not occur in China (for the bear and bunny, sewing is completed in Vietnam or the US; for the elf, sewing occurs in India). Thus, the operation group's described work of sewing cut fabric pieces together to form the unstuffed plush toy body shell was not performed in China.

The ruling states that the country of origin of the motor is Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam, and CBP held those countries as origin precisely because the motor (a component described in the operation group as a generic 3V DC motor) originated there.

The facts state that for the 'Animated Elf', the mechanical framework is manufactured and assembled in China, matching the operation group's work ('Assemble internal mechanical animation frameworks'). CBP held China as the country of origin for the plush toys, including the Animated Elf, because the major component manufacturing and framework assembly took place there.

The ruling states that the DC motors originate from Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam, and CBP held those countries (the country of origin of the motor) as an origin of the good for trade remedy purposes.

The ruling states that the country of origin of the geared DC motor is Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam, and CBP specifically held that the country of origin of the Strobe Light Animator Build Box will be Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam (the country of origin of the motor) along with China for the remaining components.

The ruling states that the country of origin of the microcontroller (Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam) was held to be one of the countries of origin for the kit, directly reflecting the work/component of the operation group (microcontrollers).

The ruling states that the country of origin of the Domino Robot Hack Pack includes Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam because that is the country of origin of the microcontroller, which directly corresponds to the operation group's work producing microcontrollers for coding/robotic build kits.

The ruling states that the remaining components (which include the wood boards, plywood trigger, guide rail, battery pack, and fasteners) originate from China, not from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam (the countries of origin of the motor that were held to be origins of the disc launcher alongside China). Moreover, these components were not among the reasons CBP found origin in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam.

The operation group describes producing plywood boards, acrylic parts, breadboards, sensors, LED strips, battery packs, wiring, and fasteners. In the ruling, the components other than the motors originate from China, but CBP held the country of origin to be Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam (based on the origin of the motor) alongside China for trade remedy purposes, with the motor being the primary origin determination component. The specific operations and extensive parts mentioned in the claim were not performed in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam, nor were they the basis for conferring origin to those countries.

The ruling states that the remaining components (which include the plywood pieces, breadboard, bolts, and wiring) originate in China, not the countries held as the origin of the kit (Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam, which was based solely on the origin of the microcontroller).

The ruling determined that the microcontroller originates in Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam, while the remaining components (which encompass the wood, plastic/PET, breadboard, LED bar, fasteners, etc.) originate in China. CBP did not hold that the work of cutting/shaping wood, fabricating acrylic/molded parts, or producing breadboards/sensors/fasteners occurred in the microcontroller origin countries (Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam) or formed the basis for conferring those countries of origin.

The components mentioned in this operation group (such as breadboards, plywood gears, wiring, fasteners, etc.) are among the 'remaining components' that originate in China, not Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam. Furthermore, CBP's holding determined origin based on the country of origin of the microcontroller (and China for the remaining components for trade remedy measures); the work of cutting/fabricating these remaining components was not done in the microcontroller origin countries, nor was it the reason CBP held those countries as origin.

The components described in the operation group (such as plywood, breadboards, wiring, etc.) originate in China, whereas the held origin for the primary component (the microcontroller) was Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam. Furthermore, CBP's holding regarding those countries was based exclusively on the origin of the microcontroller, not the wood, acrylic, or other molded kit components.

Ruling H350263 involves an unassembled build box kit where components are packaged together in a retail box without undergoing substantial transformation, resulting in CBP determining that collating and packaging the kit components does not confer a single new origin and the kit maintains the origins of its individual components.

In Ruling N343777 (scenario 1), pre-sewn plush dinosaur shells made in China were shipped to Vietnam to be stuffed with polyester fiber and plastic pellet bags, sewn closed, and labeled. CBP held that the country of origin remained China, confirming that the stuffing, closing, and labeling operations in Vietnam did not effect a substantial transformation or confer origin.

Ruling N348808 involved cut/embroidered fabric parts and frames from China sent to Vietnam, the US, or India where stuffing, sewing to completion, and assembling around mechanical frames occurred. CBP determined that the country of origin remained China for all three plush toys, confirming that these stuffing, closing, and assembly operations did not substantially transform the goods into products of Vietnam, the US, or India.

Ruling N350221 addresses a Drawing Machine Build Box kit imported unassembled, but the ruling text provided does not discuss or involve stuffing plush shells, sewing plush shells, assembling around mechanical frames, or a specific determination that kit retail packaging was not a substantial transformation as stated in the claim.

Ruling N350296 concerns an unassembled kit for a Balance Bot Hack Pack (robotics/coding kit containing a microcontroller, PCBs, motors, chassis, etc.), and does not involve stuffing plush shells, sewing plush shells closed, or assembling around mechanical frames as described in the operation group.

Ruling N350297 concerns the country of origin of an unassembled Domino Robot Hack Pack kit (involving microcontrollers, motors, dominoes, and packaging into a retail box). It does not involve filling plush shells, sewing plush shells, assembling around mechanical frames, or any other stuffing/closing operations of the operation group.

In Scenario One, the compressor assembly work (including casting the housing, machining crankshaft/cylinder head/piston, subassembly construction, lubrication, and sealing) was performed in India, which CBP held to be the country of origin for the heat pump units.

In scenarios two and three, the compressor was assembled in China using the described operations (casting housing, fabricating crankshaft/piston, subassemblies, lubrication/seals), but CBP held that the country of origin of the finished heat pump units was India, thereby demonstrating that this compressor subassembly work did not by itself confer origin on the country where it was done.

The ruling states that key components including the burner assembly, oxygen depletion sensor (ODS) assemblies, and ignitor module originated in China, which was held by CBP to be the country of origin of the finished gas heaters because the assembly in Vietnam did not result in a substantial transformation.

The ruling states that in all three scenarios, the evaporator and condenser (cooling components) are manufactured and assembled in India. CBP explicitly determined the country of origin to be India for scenarios two and three based on the fact that the majority of cooling components are from India, and for scenario one based on Indian processing of the compressor and cooling components.

The ruling held that the country of origin of the finished gas furnaces is Thailand, where final assembly and subassembly manufacturing occurred from imported components (from China and Mexico) and Thai-origin chassis parts. The claim asserts that assembly using this group's output did not make the country where it was done the origin, but CBP explicitly held that the Thailand assembly did confer origin.

In Ruling N347271, the primary and secondary heat exchangers, main control board, DC motor, exhaust fan/motor, and centrifugal fan were manufactured in China, while the burner, thermostat, special sensor, and switches were sourced in Mexico. However, CBP held that the country of origin of the finished gas furnace is Thailand, confirming that manufacturing these components in China or Mexico did not make those countries the origin of the finished product.

CBP determined that the country of origin of the finished gas furnaces was Thailand, which was the country where the product was assembled using those components/subassemblies, contradicting the claim that assembly using this group's output did not make the country where the product was assembled the origin.

The ruling states that operations such as cutting, hole punching, painting, bending, and assembling were performed in Vietnam, not China. Furthermore, the ruling does not describe the specific fabrication of chassis panels or structural metal parts as claimed, and CBP's determination that the country of origin was China was based on Chinese subassemblies and components not being substantially transformed by the assembly operations in Vietnam.

Ruling N347270 states that the top, bottom, left, right, front, and back chassis panels and various plates/brackets were manufactured in Thailand from Thai-origin steel through stamping, bending, welding, and powder coating, and this first-stage manufacturing contributed directly to the holding that the finished gas furnaces are of Thai origin.

The ruling states that in Thailand, steel is stamped, bent, welded, and powder-coated to form the chassis panels (top, bottom, left, right, front, back) as well as various fixed plates, seal plates, and support plates. CBP held that the country of origin of the finished gas furnaces is Thailand based on the substantial transformation resulting from these manufacturing stages and subassembly processes.

The ruling explicitly details that in the first stage of manufacturing in Thailand, chassis panels (top, bottom, left, right, front, and back) and structural metal parts (including fixed plates, base seal plate, and support plate) are produced from Thai-origin steel via stamping, bending, welding, and powder coating, forming essential components and subassemblies for the finished gas furnace held to be of Thai origin.

Ruling N345976 evaluated the assembly of gas heaters in Vietnam using Chinese and Vietnamese parts. Certain gas controls (gas selector valve, LP/NG regulators) were made in Vietnam, and the Vietnamese process included cutting, punching, bending, painting, and assembling with other Chinese components (including thermostatic gas valves and aluminum tubes). CBP concluded that the processing in Vietnam was not a substantial transformation and that the country of origin remained China.

Ruling N347270 describes building key subassemblies (cabinet, burner, heat exchanger, gas pipe, electric control) and integrating them with panels and remaining components, wiring, and testing in Thailand, which CBP determined was the country of origin for the gas furnaces.

The ruling states that key subassemblies (cabinet, burner, heat exchanger, gas pipe, and electric control subassemblies) are manufactured in Thailand through assembly, installing, securing, and wiring, and then assembled into finished furnaces, tested, and inspected in Thailand. This manufacturing and assembly in Thailand formed the factual basis for CBP's holding that Thailand is the country of origin.

Ruling N347272 details that key subassemblies (cabinet, burner, heat exchanger, gas pipe, electric control) and final assembly of the gas furnaces (including testing, inspection, wiring, securing, and assembling components onto Thai-stamped chassis and installation boards) occur in Thailand, which CBP determined to be the country of origin based on this substantial manufacturing and assembly process.

In scenarios one and two, final assembly occurred in China, yet CBP held the country of origin to be India for all scenarios based primarily on the manufacture of the cooling components (e.g., evaporator, condenser, compressor) rather than final assembly.

Ruling N345976 addressed gas heaters assembled in Vietnam using mostly Chinese components (including front/back panel assemblies, burner assembly, ODS assemblies, thermocouple connection wire, thermostatic gas valve, etc.) along with Vietnamese parts through cutting, hole punching, painting, bending, assembling, tightening, and testing. CBP held that the country of origin remained China, directly supporting the claim that this assembly/integration work did not confer origin on the country where it was performed.

In scenarios 1 and 2, final assembly of the heat pump units (mounting components to the base plate, enclosing compressor, evaporator, condenser, etc.) was performed in China, but CBP held the country of origin to be India, finding that final assembly in China did not confer origin.

In Ruling H332922, CBP held that the country of origin of the golf club heads is Japan because the essential forging operations that formed the billets into rough golf club heads occurred in Japan, which matches work listed in the operation group.

In Ruling N340536, CBP held that the country of origin of the golf club putter heads is Vietnam. The metal injection molding (MIM) operations—specifically mixing metallic powder with binder, injection molding, de-binding, and sintering in a vacuum furnace—occurred in Vietnam and were determined to impart the essence and country of origin of the putter heads.

Ruling N346303 determined that the country of origin of the golf club driver heads is Vietnam, where raw titanium and stainless steel were melted and cast into wax-molded hard-shell clusters and deshelled into individual club heads before being sent to China for finishing operations.

Ruling H350263 evaluated an unassembled disc launcher build box kit where the motor originates in Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam, and CBP held that the country of origin of the disc launcher will be Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam (the country of origin of the motor) alongside China for the other components. Producing DC motors is part of the operation group's work and was the direct basis for CBP's determination of origin for those countries.

For the 'Animated Elf', the ruling states that the mechanical framework was manufactured and assembled in China, matching the operation group's work ('Assemble internal mechanical animation frameworks'). CBP held that China is the country of origin for the Animated Elf.

The operation group includes the manufacture of DC motors. In ruling N350221, CBP determined that for purposes of trade remedies, the country of origin of the kit is Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam specifically because that is the country of origin of the motors.

The ruling states that the country of origin of the Strobe Light Animator Build Box will be Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, or Vietnam based on the country of origin of the motor (which matches the work of manufacturing DC/geared motors in the operation group).

CBP held the countries of origin of the Balance Bot Hack Pack to be Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam based on the country of origin of the microcontroller, which is manufactured in those countries as described in the operation group.

The operation group includes the manufacture of microcontrollers, and the ruling specifically identifies Taiwan, Italy, Malaysia, or Vietnam as the country of origin of the microcontroller (which in turn determines the held country of origin for the Domino Robot Hack Pack alongside China for the remaining components).

Ruling H338127 describes front-end processing in the United States that includes single crystal growth of a silicon carbide ingot/boule from a seed crystal and powder, slicing the ingot with a diamond multi-wire cutting saw, and double-sided grinding and polishing to control thickness variation, bow, and warp. CBP held that the country of origin of the silicon carbide Schottky diode is the United States based on these front-end processing operations occurring in the United States.

Ruling N333934 states that monocrystalline silicon wafer production and wafer fabrication occur in South Korea, and CBP held the country of origin of the integrated circuits to be South Korea based on the manufacturing operations performed there impart the essential functional character before shipment to China.

The ruling states that front-end manufacturing steps conducted in the United States include Single Crystal Growth, Slicing the Silicon Carbide Ingot, and Grinding and Polishing of the Wafer. CBP held the country of origin to be the United States based on these front-end wafer fabrication processes occurring in the United States.

The ruling notes that substrate construction (producing silicon substrates/empty wafers) takes place in South Korea, followed by front-end fabrication operations in South Korea. CBP determined that the country of origin is South Korea because substantial transformation occurs during the South Korean manufacturing stages and not in China.

The facts state that the manufacturing of the single crystal silicon wafer (bare wafer) occurs in Japan, along with the formation of the circuit elements and dicing. CBP held the country of origin to be Japan because the essential character/circuitry was imparted in Japan and not substantially transformed in China.

In Ruling N334417, the SiC bare substrate was manufactured in China, but CBP held that subsequent processing in Japan substantially transformed the bare substrate into an epitaxial wafer, conferring Japan as the country of origin rather than China where the bare wafer substrate was produced.

The ruling states that epitaxial deposition is part of the front-end semiconductor wafer fabrication process occurring in South Korea, where each chip obtains its completed integrated circuit functionality. Because the subsequent processing in China does not result in a substantial transformation, CBP held South Korea to be the country of origin based on the fabrication processes (including epitaxial deposition) performed there.

The ruling states that epitaxial film deposition and the control of film thickness, dopant concentration, and dislocation density take place in Japan, which CBP determined to be the country of origin because this process substantially transforms the Chinese bare substrate into the epitaxial wafer.

Ruling N337307 explicitly states that 'Epigrowth - HTCVD' is one of the front-end manufacturing steps performed in the United States, which was held to be the country of origin because all front-end manufacturing steps for the finished die take place there.

The ruling states that front-end operations performed in South Korea (the determined country of origin) include epitaxial growth (processing empty wafers through automated silicon epitaxial film growth equipment) followed by fabrication, after which the wafers contain fully functional silicon metal-oxide semiconductors. CBP determined origin is South Korea because substantial transformation occurs during front-end wafer manufacturing there rather than during packaging/assembly in China.

The ruling states that wafer fabrication operations (Thin-Film deposition, Photolithography, Etching, and Ion implantation) took place in South Korea, imparting the completed integrated circuit functionality. Because the subsequent processing in China did not result in a substantial transformation, CBP determined South Korea was the country of origin.

Ruling N337307 specifically states that all front-end manufacturing steps for the finished die—including photolithography (photoresist, exposure, developing), etching, ion implantation, and chip probing—take place in the United States, which CBP held as the country of origin before the wafer is sent to China for backend assembly.

In Ruling N343494, CBP determined that the country of origin of the discrete power transistors and transistor power modules is the United States. CBP found that the front-end fabrication processes performed in the United States (including epitaxy, ion implantation, layer deposition, lithography, etching, etc.) impart the essential character and operational capability to the transistor dice, and that subsequent processing and testing in Malaysia and China do not result in a substantial transformation.

According to the facts of Ruling N344105, front-end operations (including fabrication steps such as oxide deposition, photolithography, etching, ion implantation, and metal deposition, as well as electrical testing) take place at onsemi's South Korean manufacturing facility, resulting in fully functional semiconductors. CBP held South Korea to be the country of origin because substantial transformation did not occur in China during subsequent back-end operations.

The ruling states that wafer manufacturing, including element formation (transistors, wiring, protective films) and probe inspection, takes place in Japan, and CBP held the country of origin to be Japan because the subsequent packaging operations in China did not result in a substantial transformation.

The ruling states that front-end manufacturing processes take place in the United States and include oxide/nitride/metal deposition, photolithography, etching, and on-wafer testing. CBP determined the country of origin is the United States because these front-end wafer fabrication steps impart the essential character and make the diodes functional, whereas back-end processing in China does not result in a substantial transformation.

In Ruling N343494, front-end wafer fabrication took place in the United States and was held to establish the country of origin as the United States, directly contradicting the claim that front-end fabrication did not confer origin.

Ruling N333934 involved growing copper pillars, back grinding, and cutting into individual die (along with flip-chip assembly and packing) in China on wafers fabricated in South Korea. CBP determined that the Chinese manufacturing/assembly process did not result in a substantial transformation and held that the country of origin remained South Korea.

The ruling evaluated a silicon carbide MOSFET where front-end fabrication occurred in the United States and back-end manufacturing—including wafer mounting and sawing (dicing), die attach, wire bonding, molding, and testing—took place in China. CBP held that the country of origin remained the United States, confirming that the back-end processing (which encompasses wafer dicing and packaging assembly) did not confer origin on China.

In Ruling N345881, the dicing (cutting from the wafer mounted on tape) occurred in Japan, where the wafer fabrication took place, and the ruling evaluated assembly/packaging in China (die bond, wire bond, mold, etc.). It did not evaluate whether wafer thinning, bumping, and dicing conferred origin or constituted a substantial transformation.

The ruling does not describe the specific operation group described ('grow copper pillar bumps on the front side of the wafer; back-grind the wafer to reduce thickness; mount the wafer on tape and saw or dice it into individual semiconductor die'). Rather, wafer thinning occurred during front-end processing in the United States, bumping is not mentioned at all, and China's back-end assembly involved wafer mounting, sawing into individual die, wire bonding, and encapsulation.

Ruling N333934 involved back-end assembly processes performed in China (bumping, grinding, cutting die, flip-chip attachment to substrate, and packing) on semiconductor wafers fabricated in South Korea. CBP determined that these Chinese manufacturing/assembly processes did not effect a substantial transformation, and held that the country of origin remained South Korea.

Ruling N337307 evaluated the country of origin of a MOSFET where all front-end manufacturing was performed in the United States and back-end manufacturing (die attach, wire bonding, molding, plating, trim & form, testing, marking, packaging) occurred in China. CBP held that the country of origin was the United States, thereby ruling that the back-end die packaging and testing operations in China did not confer origin.

Ruling N343494 addresses back-end packaging operations (attaching die to lead frame, reflow soldering, wire bonding, molding, and testing) performed in China and Malaysia on US-fabricated transistor dice. CBP held that these back-end operations do not constitute a substantial transformation, determining the country of origin to be the United States.

Ruling N344105 evaluated the back-end packaging and testing operations in China (dicing, attaching the transistor within the package using wires and pins, encapsulating in plastic molding, and testing) and determined that these operations did not substantially transform the product. Thus, China was not the country of origin; instead, CBP held that the country of origin was South Korea, where the front-end fabrication occurred.

In Ruling N345881, the Chinese manufacturing processes consisted of die bond, wire bond, mold, tie bar cut, laser mark, cut bend, characteristics inspection, visual inspection, and packing/shipping. CBP held that these back-end packaging and testing operations in China did not effect a substantial transformation and that the country of origin remained Japan, where the wafer fabrication occurred.

In Ruling N347890, CBP held that back-end processing (dicing, attaching die to carrier, wire bonding, molding, singulation) performed in China did not effect a substantial transformation of the US-fabricated RF FEM integrated circuit dice, and determined the country of origin remained the United States.
